title: Detection of signals in presence of noise through Josephson junction switching currents
authors: O. V. Pountougnigni, R. Yamapi, C. Tchawoua, V. Pierro, G. Filatrella
abstract: Josephson junctions can be employed to reveal a sinusoidal signal in presence of Gaussian noise. To mimic realistic setups, the detection is performed linearly ramping the bias current until a switch to the finite voltage occurs; the analysis of the resulting switching currents can be exploited to decide about the presence of the harmonic drive. The signal is applied in two conditions: with an unknown initial phase (incoherent strategy) and with a known initial phase (coherent strategy). In both conditions, the analysis of the efficiency of the detection, performed through the signal-to-noise ratio, as estimated by the Kumar-Carrol index, shows that the dependence upon the Josephson junction ramp rate is beneficial, especially for relatively fast speed. One can conclude that the collection of the switching currents is a robust technique, and thus it is possible to exploit the advantages of a predetermined finite time to collect the data.
summary: This work investigates using Josephson junction switching currents to detect weak sinusoidal signals buried in Gaussian noise. By analyzing the switching times under controlled bias ramps, the authors quantify detection performance using the K-C index. They conclude that this switching current collection method is robust, showing that faster ramp rates enhance the signal detection capability.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of detecting a weak sinusoidal signal embedded within significant Gaussian noise using the switching currents of a Josephson junction (JJ).
main_result: The analysis demonstrates that collecting the switching currents as the bias current is ramped is a robust detection technique, with performance improving significantly for faster ramp rates.
method: The detection efficiency is quantified using the Kumar-Carrol index (K-C index), which estimates the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) by analyzing the average and variance of the switching times.
model_or_system: The physical system is an underdamped Josephson junction modeled by a Langevin equation. The analysis involves simulating the junction's dynamics under a time-dependent bias ramp, incorporating both signal and noise terms.
key_observables: Switching currents/times ($	au_{sw}$), Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) estimated by the K-C index ($d_{KC}$), and the dependence of these metrics on the ramp rate ($v$) and driving frequency ($\omega$).
important_parameters: The analysis explores the effects of the bias ramp rate ($v$), the signal amplitude ($\gamma_{ac}$), and the driving frequency ($\omega$).
main_assumptions: The K-C index is used as a proxy for SNR, and the analysis relies on the resistively shunted and capacitively junction model.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of the K-C index and average switching time on the driving frequency ($\omega$) for both coherent and incoherent strategies, and show how these metrics change as a function of the bias ramp speed ($v$).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the governing Langevin equation for the JJ. It then details the two detection strategies (coherent vs. incoherent) and uses the K-C index to quantify performance. The core of the work analyzes how the ramp rate affects this detection capability, concluding that faster ramps are beneficial.
why_interesting: The use of nonlinear, dissipative quantum devices (JJs) as sensitive detectors for weak signals in noisy environments is highly relevant to quantum sensing and measurement theory, bridging condensed matter physics with signal processing.
